maria: quick heads-up: noticed a latency regression on canary for llama-3-13b serving chat-style traffic. p50 up ~18% on 1k-token streaming runs.

ben: which pool and selector config? any traces?

maria: dedicated pool-3 (g4dn-like), kernel selector enabled. traces show selector choosing a scalar GEMM fallback for some calls. snippet:

```
[perf] op=attn qk_mul kernel=matmul_fallback time=3.3ms calls=410
[perf] op=attn qk_mul kernel=fast_qkv_batched time=0.92ms calls=1600
[kselector] model=llama3-13b reasons=[activation_unfused, metadata_mismatch]
```

maria: also saw repeated KV cache re-warms around ~512 and 1024 token boundaries. suspect rope_theta/runtime defaults + chat template causing high position indices and eviction churn.

sasha: can you paste the model config you used?

maria: model config excerpt:
```
hidden_size: 5120
num_attention_heads: 40
head_dim: 128
norm: RMSNorm
activation: SiLU
rope_theta: null
chat_prefix_len: 36
```

ben: head_dim matches but selector flagged activation_unfused. our Linux x86 builds have fused RMSNorm+GELU kernels; SiLU falls back to slower elementwise path if fused kernel missing. combined with selector.threshold bump on canary this explains conservative picks.

kai: infra-bot: canary roll 2026-03-12 -> 2026-03-14 included `kernel_selector.threshold=0.9` (was 0.75). made selector more conservative.

sasha: two paths: add fused SiLU kernel into runtime builds (longer work), or override model metadata in canary to force vector kernels / prefer fast_qkv path. also check that chat template preprocessing isn't inserting extra reshapes that break kernel fast-path shapes.

maria: repro command I ran:
```
serve --model=llama3-13b --kernel-selector=auto --max_batch_tokens=4096 --latency_slo_ms=120
ab -n 1000 -c 8 POST /v1/chat
```

maria: quick micro-experiments:
- forcing `rope_theta=10000` reduced observed KV re-warm events by ~12% (less index drift, fewer heuristic-evictions)
- setting `kernel_selector.force_vector=true` bumped fast_qkv_batched selection to ~92% and p50 returned near baseline

ben: p95 still high for very long requests (>2k tokens)? likely batching scheduler and slot starvation when large sequences arrive — makes tail worse.

sasha: propose changes:
- runtime: add long-sequence fast-path: route requests >1024 tokens to a prewarmed pool with relaxed batching (max_batch_tokens_long=8192, min_batch_tokens=128)
- runtime: expose `kv_evict_threshold` per-model so we don't evict aggressively for chat templates with long prefixes
- infra: temporary revert of selector.threshold bump for pool-3 or model exception
- build: add fused SiLU kernel test and plan rollout

ben: agree. action items assigned:
- kai/infra: rollback or exception (kai)
- sasha/eng-ml: SiLU fused kernel + unit test for template reshape (sasha)
- maria: push canary model override with rope_theta=10000 + kernel_selector.force_vector and run perf suite
- runtime: scheduler change for long-seq fast-path (ben)

kai: infra-bot: rollback scheduled for pool-3 in 30m window. notifying ops.

maria: canary results posted: p50 ~ baseline, p95 improved ~9% (prev 260ms -> 238ms). kernel traces show `fast_qkv_batched` selected ~92% of calls. will attach logs/reproducer in a follow-up.

ben: please add reproducer script and minimal config to test-suite so this doesn't regress again.

sasha: small PR incoming to assert chat prefix handling doesn't add extra reshapes that affect kernel selection.

maria: thanks folks :thumbsup: will update once long-seq fast-path bench is in.
